lines.en: Some nights, I try to separate myself from the outside world. I have done enough damage already.
And in this world, where more things are broken than most even realize, the traces of my involvement still act as beacons illuminating the night sky with the flames of my misguided passion.

My appetite for destruction, even. That subtle, hidden craving within me, constantly poking and prodding me to bite not the hand that feeds but the hands of those who sit beneath it with their mouths agape.
Each and every one of us is seeking salvation. And whether that be in religious contexts or not matters little when everything is bigger under the lens of a magnifying glass.
Tonight is not one of those nights. But tonight is still different.
For as I tap a green circle on a small box that keeps me connected to everything, I reach deep into my chest cavity and remove something I only take out for special occasions.
It’s a roll of metaphorical duct tape. And a small bottle of miraculous human glue.

These are things I will hold in my hands as someone else repairs what I can not — but I will deceive myself into thinking I have helped by standing to their side and pretending to know what is happening.
Forgive me Father, for she has sinned.
: Hello?
: Akira, yo. Heard you’re kinda famous now. Surprised you still picked up the phone.
: Anything for my favorite recovering addict slash cancer patient. I’m going to charge you if you’re looking for an autograph, though.
: How much? I’ve got an endless piggy bank now that I’ve been sucked back into Nee-sama’s shit. Need a little more than an autograph, though.
: Then you’re in luck because my body is on permanent discount and I imagine that’s what you want instead.
: Wrong again. Just need you to come with me on a little...errand.

: Oh no. We’re not burying a body, are we? Is it Tsukasa’s? It was only a matter of time until Tsubasa found a new way to address the problem that is her existence. At least she isn’t heavy. Fine. I’m in.
: You done?
: Sorry. One of us has to be funny and I know it isn’t going to be you. You’re too cool and sad for that.
: Okay, well I’m outside your house right now and you should get out here if you know what’s good for you.
: If I don’t, will you break in and beat up my daughter? She could use it and I’m too weak to ever actually stand up to her.
: Just fuckin’ come outside and humor me for a little, won’t ya? Without makin’ any more jokes.
: Well that doesn’t sound very humorous at all.
: Make me wait any longer and I’m coming in there to kick your ass instead of your daughter’s.
: You act like I wouldn’t like that.
: Ten more seconds or I’m calling Tsubasa.
: Hi.
: Damn. You really are afraid of her, huh?
: I’m afraid of anyone with money. Plus, no one with boobs that big ever uses their powers for good.
: Would say you’re wrong on account of the whole payin’ for my treatment shit. But I guess takin’ steps to put me back out on the street ain’t exactly doing society any favors.
: Anyway, hop on. We’re going for a ride.
: Sure. I’ve more or less gotten over my fear of your motorcycle by now. I’d still like to know where we’re going, though.
: Somewhere I should’ve gone a long fuckin’ time ago, that’s where.
: Rehab?
: Oh, right. Forgot that was even a thing.
: But also, no. We’re goin’ to Sara’s place so I can apologize for being such a fuck up.
: Oh. Well, why do you need me for that?
: I guess I don’t need you. But you were there when shit went to hell, so it seems only fair you should be there when that chapter is closed too.

: Plus, even I ain’t dumb enough to ride into battle alone. Apart from...all the times I’ve ridden into battle alone. But this is like...a feelings battle. I don’t think I can use violence to make Sara forgive me.
: You probably could with handcuffs and a whip or something. I think she might actually like that.
: Get on the fucking bike, Akira.
: Fine, jeez. Just be careful driving around here. The roads are steep and- ah?!
: Hang on, douche monkey! Only got so long before I need to be back at the manor!
Yuki tears through the streets, almost killing several pedestrians in the process, but she somehow narrowly avoids them and only gives me a minor heart attack as a result.
It’s fine, though. Because it’s nothing a little alcohol and two miniature green-eyed girls can’t fix.

Assuming this doesn’t get all sad and everyone winds up crying or something. Which is probably possible given the context. Just I don’t want to think about that, so I’ll imagine everyone is naked instead.
: Mmm...boobs.
: Can’t tell if I went so fast that I gave you brain damage or if you just came with it already installed.
: Shut up. You’re interrupting my fantasy.
: Hey! Welcome to- oh.
: It’s just you...
: Uhh...hi.
: This is...somewhat...unexpected.
: Yeah...uhh...hey.
: Sorry for not callin’ ahead of time or anything, but...I wanted to drop by and, like...you know.
: Wh...Where is everybody?
: This is everybody. We’ve been in a steady decline ever since a certain bartender decided to stop showing up.
: When did you dye your hair? I like it.
: Don’t give her any compliments, Sana.
: Sorry. I meant I don’t like it.
: That’s more like it. You need to be careful with girls like her, Sana. You show the faintest sign of weakness or affection and they just take advantage of you. Isn’t that right, Yuki?
: Sara...you know I’m...here to apologize, right?
: Oh, are you? Excuse me for not realizing it.
: It’s just that most people normally apologize within a year of doing something wrong and you decided to cut me out entirely. So you can get lost for all I care.
: Can I...get you a drink, Sensei? I feel like...the two of us should maybe...try to stay out of this, if possible...
: You’re affected by this too, Sana. So if you’d also like to yell at Yuki for all of the extra hours you’ve been forced to work because of her, I won’t mind at all.
: I mean...I basically just...went back to the same schedule I was...working before she was here, so...
: Ahem.
: S...Sorry...What I meant to say is...you’re a bitch and...I hate you...
: I will take a beer, Sana. But I’d like it over there in the corner of the room so I can get out of the blast radius.
: Oh, thank god.
: Sara-
: Hmph.
: Can we please, just...talk? I won’t take long. And I don’t expect you to forgive me or anything, I’ve just...got some shit I need to say.
: Well, I don’t. I’ve already said all there is to say to you. And I’m not going to let you trick me into caring again knowing you’ll just throw me away the second you find it convenient.

: I ain’t trying to trick you. And you can throw me out whenever the fuck you want. But at least give me the chance to talk some shit about myself first. It ain’t fair if you’re hoggin’ all the negativity.
: I gave you plenty of chances, Yuki. Far more chances than anyone should have given you.
: And you know what that did for me? Nothing but heartbreak and betrayal and finding out that people like you really are all the same at the end of the day.
: You just take and take until there’s nothing left and then vanish like it never mattered at all.
: So why should I waste my precious time on someone who’s already made it known they don’t give a shit about me? Huh?
: You ain’t gotta do anything if you don’t want to. And you’ve got every right to hate me right now...
: But I’ve realized lately just how fast life moves by, and I don’t want to leave this place without apologizing to you first.
: Oh, cry me a river. You’re making it sound like you’re dying or something when we all know you’re just desperate for money again and-
: Sara, I’ve got cancer.
: It ain’t, like...a death sentence or anything. But it’s made me start lookin’ at shit a little differently and...I don’t know...
: I just want to say sorry for everything...
: But if you really don’t want me here, I’ll just-
: Sana.
: Watch the bar for me.
: I’m sorry, Yuki. I...didn’t know.
: Ain’t nothin’ you need to apologize for. That’s why I came here, remember?
: I know, but...I at least could have been a little kinder with my words if I knew.
: Is it...bad?
: Well, it definitely ain’t good. But I’m seeing doctors and shit, so...trying to stay optimistic.
: I’m sorry, but...if you need money, I don’t have much to spare and-
: Huh? No, I...No, no, no, no, no, no. That’s not it at all. I don’t need money. That ain’t why I’m here.
: But...the whole reason you started working here in the first place was because you were broke. What do you mean you don’t need money?
: I’ve got a friend with more cash than she knows what to do with. And she’s payin’ for everything. Even gave me a place to live and...
: I’m doin’ better now. I still ain’t perfect, but I’m better. Just...remains to be seen how long it’ll last this time and...if I even will last. You know?
: Yuki...if you’re just saying all of this so I won’t have to worry, it’s not going to work. I might be mad at you, but I still care.
: I know...You took a chance on me when nobody else would. And I ain’t ever gonna forget that, no matter how fucked up on drugs or anything else I get.

: This ain’t a lie, though. And I know that probably don’t mean much, but it really ain’t. Could even have her confirm it if you really want me to. Just...want to avoid that if possible since she can be a lot too.
: And you trust her? Because this is a big deal, Yuki. This is your life we’re talking about.
: I trust her, yeah. Known her for...damn, over half of my life now. Time really flies, huh?
: Yeah...it really does.
: Anyway, I didn’t come here to try and make you feel bad for me or anything. I just wanted to apologize for the whole...relapsing and...ghosting the bar ordeal. I know you needed the help.
: Yuki, wha...no! That was never the issue! Do you really think that’s what you need to apologize for?! Do you think that’s why I’m so upset?!
: Uhhhhhhh...no? But just so we’re both on the same page, can you tell me why you are?
: Because you wouldn’t let me be there for you when you needed it most! You basically told me to go fuck myself for caring about you! Do you not understand how much that hurts?!
: And I know you had your reasons! My parents were raging alcoholics and I understand addiction. But it’s because I understand it that I can’t be around people who don’t want to fight back!
: I never expected you to stay clean forever. And if you want to say that’s fucked up on my part or whatever, fine. I guess it kind of is. That’s just the way this works, though.
: But if you’re going to be fighting two diseases now instead of just one, you need to understand that when people that care about you reach out to help, it’s not because they’re looking for a cure.
: It’s because they don’t want to watch you suffer. And they’re willing to sacrifice a little of their own happiness if it means letting you feel it.
: That’s why I’m sad. Because you rejected me.
: And I’m sure you think you were just saving me pain by doing that, but you only wound up making it worse by subjecting me to watch as you torched everything you worked so hard for.
: Damn...I can’t even be a fuck-up without fucking it up. I didn’t know you felt that way, Sara. Never realized...how much you cared, I guess.
: Then apologize for that. Because that’s the apology I want. A job is just a job. There are bars all over Kumon-mi, but there’s only one of you.

: I’m sorry, Sara. I really am. For...everything. Apologizing for just one thing feels like it ain’t nearly enough. So...guess I’ll apologize for apologizin’ about stuff you don’t want me to apologize for too. That work?
: Yeah...
: That works...
: Don’t you fuckin’ cry on me, idiot. I ain’t done shit to earn those tears.
: Stop thinking you need to earn everything and just take what people are willing to give you. You’re so...fucking annoying sometimes.
: Also, please don’t die. I’m not good with funerals.
: I’ll do my best.
: Been fightin’ my whole life. Kinda fucked up how I even considered stopping for this one when it’s the biggest challenge yet.
: How long have you known?...
: Since about...five hours before I relapsed, maybe? When was that? I can’t remember for reasons you’re probably aware of already.
: Was that why?...
: It was.
: But if it wasn’t that, it would’ve been somethin’ else eventually. You said it yourself. That’s just how this works.
: That’s just how this works...
: I’ll need you to clock in an hour early tomorrow.
: Wait, what?
: You heard me. Don’t think I’ll be cutting your hours just because you have cancer.
: But...I didn’t ask for the job back. I don’t need the job anymore.
: Oh? So you work one part-time job and then escape the workforce entirely all because you have some rich friend? Sorry, Yuki. I just figured you might want some sort of purpose in life.
: The fuck is this? You didn’t even want to see me like thirty minutes ago. Now you’re forcin’ me to come back to work?
: Yes. You owe me. And if you really want to show me you’re sorry, you’ll work for free for your first month back. Understood?
: I mean...I do understand. But-

: But what? You hate me and only came here to tie up loose ends before spending the rest of your life waiting for death? Because that’s how I’ll interpret anything but, “Okay, Sara. I’ll clock in early tomorrow.”
: This feels sorta like emotional blackmail.
: Well, Yuki, that’s because it is.
: Wow. I...I didn’t realize you had it in you.
: Guess I’ll just...clock in early tomorrow. Not sure how I’m going to explain this to Nee-sama, though.
: Nee-sama, huh? I don’t think I’ve heard you address someone that formally before. Should I be jealous?
: I don’t think so. But she’s sure as fuck about to be jealous of you since it means I’m spending less time on her leash.
: Sounds to me like I should invest in a leash as well, then.
: Sounds to me like I’m due for another relapse.
: Sounds to me like I should invest in a cage too.
: Please don’t. I’m already trapped in one.
